description: A table function in a comma-separated FROM list is implicitly LATERAL in Snowflake - it may reference columns of the tables written BEFORE it, and the LATERAL keyword is optional. The ubiquitous FROM t, TABLE(FLATTEN(input => t.col)) f form was executed once with no lateral context, so the correlated reference failed with 'Column not found'; only the explicit LATERAL FLATTEN spelling worked. The lateral may also reference a SELECT-LIST ALIAS of the same query, which is not a column of any FROM table - and a REAL column of the same name wins over such an alias. After an explicit JOIN the per-row context must follow the COMBINED row's layout, not the alias map's hash order, or the lateral reads the wrong slots and silently empties the query. A bare JOIN to a table function, with no LATERAL keyword and no ON, still correlates to the left row. Correlation is per row, so N source rows with M elements each produce N*M rows, an empty source yields none, and a table function referencing nothing outside itself still cross-joins. Converted 1:1 from query/ImplicitLateralTableFunctionTest (now retired); the Java counted rows for eleven of its seventeen tests, and the converted tests name the rows.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE stage (id INTEGER, src VARIANT)
INSERT INTO stage SELECT 1, PARSE_JSON('{"a":{"n":"first"},"b":{"n":"second"}}')
INSERT INTO stage SELECT 2, PARSE_JSON('{"a":{"n":"only"}}')
SELECT id, ex.value:n::VARCHAR AS extra_name FROM stage s, TABLE(FLATTEN(ARRAY_CONSTRUCT_COMPACT(src:a, src:b), OUTER => TRUE)) AS ex ORDER BY id, extra_name
CREATE TABLE stage2 (id INTEGER, src VARIANT)
INSERT INTO stage2 SELECT 1, PARSE_JSON('{"a":{"n":"x"},"b":{"n":"y"}}')
SELECT id, f.value:n::VARCHAR AS nm FROM stage2 s, LATERAL FLATTEN(input => ARRAY_CONSTRUCT_COMPACT(src:a, src:b)) f ORDER BY nm
CREATE TABLE stage3 (id INTEGER, src VARIANT)
INSERT INTO stage3 SELECT 1, PARSE_JSON('[{"n":"fromColumn"}]')
SELECT id, f.value:n::VARCHAR AS v FROM stage3 s, TABLE(FLATTEN(input => src)) f
CREATE TABLE orders (oid INTEGER, aid INTEGER)
INSERT INTO orders VALUES (10, 1)
CREATE TABLE vendors2 (aid INTEGER, plans VARIANT)
INSERT INTO vendors2 SELECT 1, PARSE_JSON('{"GOLD":{"ok":1},"SILVER":{"ok":0}}')
SELECT f.oid, l.key FROM orders f INNER JOIN vendors2 a ON a.aid = f.aid, LATERAL FLATTEN(input => a.plans) l WHERE l.key = 'GOLD'

INSERT INTO d2 SELECT 1, ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('p', 'q'), 2
SELECT f.value::VARCHAR FROM oc JOIN d2 ON oc.k = d2.k, LATERAL FLATTEN(d2.pairs) f ORDER BY 1
CREATE TABLE oc (k INTEGER, v VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO oc VALUES (1, 'x')
CREATE TABLE d2 (k INTEGER, pairs ARRAY, sz INTEGER)
INSERT INTO d2 SELECT 1, ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('p', 'q'), 2
SELECT f.value::VARCHAR FROM oc JOIN d2 USING (k), LATERAL FLATTEN(pairs) f WHERE d2.sz > 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT f.value::VARCHAR FROM oc JOIN d2 USING (k), TABLE(FLATTEN(d2.pairs)) f ORDER BY 1

CREATE TABLE jb (k INTEGER, attrs OBJECT)
INSERT INTO jb SELECT 1, OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('tags', ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('a', 'b'))
INSERT INTO jb SELECT 2, OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('tags', ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('c'))
INSERT INTO jb SELECT 3, OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('other', 1)
SELECT k, value::VARCHAR AS tag FROM jb JOIN TABLE(FLATTEN(attrs:tags)) WHERE attrs:tags IS NOT NULL ORDER BY k, tag
